sections.h2: What is the Richmond County Register of Deeds responsible for?
sections.html:
The office in Rockingham holds the deeds, deeds of trust, plats, marriage records and birth and death certificates for Richmond County, and it records new ones as they come in. When you sell, it is the stop where your deed to the buyer joins the permanent record.

Its FAQ stresses that everything on file is public. A buyer, a title examiner or a curious neighbor can all ask for copies by paying the usual fees, so assume any deed you sign will be read by others.

The date of recording is what counts, because G.S. 47-18 gives a conveyance priority over lien creditors and later buyers only from the time it is registered in the county.

sections.h2: Where is the office, and what are its recording hours in Rockingham?
sections.html:
Walk into 114 E. Franklin Street, Room 101, Rockingham, NC 28379. The county gives that as both the physical and mailing address, with 910-997-8250 as the phone line.

Hours differ by service, so read the table before choosing a delivery time. The FAQ adds that papers presented after 4:30 pm are recorded first on the following day.

If your closing runs late, ask whether your attorney's firm sends documents electronically, since that channel shuts half an hour sooner.

sections.h2: What will a Richmond County deed filing cost?
sections.html:
The office FAQ quotes $26 for a deed up to 15 pages and $4 for each page after that, which follows the uniform schedule in G.S. 161-10.

  • Loan documents run on a larger base of $64 for the first 35 pages.
  • Recording a payoff cancellation costs nothing.
  • Survey plats are $21 a sheet.
  • A certified copy begins at $5, with $2 per added page.

A plain copy of a deed or plat picked up at the counter is 35 cents per copy under the FAQ. To get one by mail, send your name and the approximate year the property was acquired.

sections.h2: How is the excise tax on a Richmond County deed collected?
sections.html:
The seller pays it into the register's office as part of the filing. The statute sets a dollar for every $500 of the price or value, counting a partial $500 as a whole one, and G.S. 105-228.30 says it must be paid before recording.

The money is divided equally between the county general fund and the state. Your settlement statement from the closing attorney should list this line, and you can compare it with the sale price yourself.

sections.h2: Can the Richmond County office fix the names on a deed?
sections.html:
The staff will record a corrected deed but will not draft it. The FAQ says a new deed must be prepared, signed, notarized and presented to the office, and it points owners to an attorney for the drafting.

Situations where this comes up before a sale include:

  • A spouse added or removed after a marriage or divorce.
  • An heir who needs to appear on title after a death.
  • Co-owners who want to sell to one buyer together.

Each of these needs the right signatures on the new deed, and each takes time to arrange. Sorting this out early keeps a closing date from slipping. Sellers who would rather not repair title issues sometimes look for a buyer who will take the property as it stands, but the recording step is identical either way.

sections.h2: How do you get a deed or plat copy, or a notary oath, in Richmond County?
sections.html:
Visit Room 101 and give your name plus roughly the year the property was acquired, or mail a request. A plat can be requested as long as it was surveyed and recorded.

Notary oaths need no appointment. Any staff member can administer one during office hours.

Because the whole file is public, you can also look up your own mortgage cancellation after a payoff to confirm that the lien came off. Ask your closing attorney to run the title search again if anything looks odd, and compare tax status with the Richmond County tax office.

sections.h2: What else gets filed with a Richmond County sale?
sections.html:
A deed is rarely the only paper. G.S. 47-18 says options, contracts to convey, leases over three years and rights of first refusal or first offer also depend on registration for their force against lien creditors and later buyers. Priority follows time order of registration.

  • A seller-financed contract for deed must be recorded, or a memorandum of it, within five business days under Chapter 47H.
  • A buyer's mortgage is filed as a deed of trust.
  • Surveys come in as plats.

Ask your attorney to list each document that will be filed, so none is held back.

sections.h2: What if the Richmond County house is in foreclosure or an inherited estate?
sections.html:
Those matters sit with the clerk of superior court rather than the register. A power-of-sale foreclosure is heard by the clerk, with notice of the hearing served at least 10 days ahead under G.S. 45-21.16.

After a sale is reported, a ten-day window opens for an upset bid, which must exceed the prior bid by at least 5 percent, with a minimum raise of $750, and each new bid restarts the ten days. Final rights attach only when no higher bid arrives in time.

A small estate may use an affidavit if personal property after liens is $20,000 or less. It goes to the clerk where the decedent lived and lists each tract of real estate. The deed that follows is still recorded here.

sections.h2: What should Richmond County sellers do before recording?
sections.html:
Rockingham is the county seat, and the office does not turn anyone away for being a stranger to it: the FAQ says anyone may obtain copies on payment of the proper fees. You may also telephone during working hours with questions about a filing.

Ask the closing attorney for the expected recording date and for the satisfaction of your old mortgage. After closing, search the county records for both and keep the recorded copies.

The property tax lien attaches on the listing date, so the year's bill follows the parcel until it is paid. Confirm the amount with the tax office. Both the excise tax and the recording charge are collected here before filing, and the return address on the filing should be one where the recorded original will reach you.

faqs.q: What hours does the Richmond County Register of Deeds record documents?
faqs.a: Counter recording stops at 4:30 PM, and e-Recording stops at 4:00 PM. Staff stay until 5:00 PM, but anything presented after 4:30 is recorded first thing the following day, so a late closing can push your recording date back.

faqs.q: Where is the Richmond County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: At 114 E. Franklin Street, Room 101, Rockingham, NC 28379, which is also its mailing address. The county lists 910-997-8250 for questions, and the FAQ invites callers during business hours.

faqs.q: What does a copy of a deed cost at the Richmond County office?
faqs.a: The office FAQ lists 35 cents per copy in person. Certified copies follow the state schedule, $5 for the first page and $2 for each page after.

faqs.q: Do I book a time to record a deed in Richmond County?
faqs.a: Nothing on the county page asks for an appointment. Bring the signed, notarized deed during recording hours, or have an eligible submitter e-record it before 4:00 PM.

faqs.q: Will the register of deeds write my deed?
faqs.a: No. The deed has to be prepared by an attorney or by the owner, then signed, notarized and brought in for recording. The office records the document and does not advise on what it should say.
